issues.summary: colony-exec/src/lib.rs mixes a scripting value interpreter with the Executor command-execution orchestrator in 4584 lines
evidence: Lines 78-1599: EvalValue enum, eval_binary, eval_expression_in_context, eval_func_call, eval_method_call, is_truthy, eval_value_equals — a complete mini-interpreter for the 'var' declaration language

Lines 2203-4548: Executor struct with 100+ methods covering simple command dispatch, pipeline execution, function/proc calls, trap execution, special file loading, heartbeat polling, reflection, and subshell management

eval_func_call (lines 775-1159, ~385 lines) and eval_method_call (lines 1162-1475, ~313 lines) implement the same ~20 operations (len, join, split, keys, values, get, has, upper, lower, trim, replace, contains, first, last, push, pop, insert, remove, slice) as parallel match arms — neither belongs in lib.rs alongside Executor
Mechanical scan shows lib.rs has complexity_score 1473, highest in the codebase, and is in the wide_param_bags list with 280 config_bag_mentions — both signals consistent with mixed concerns
issues.suggestion: Extract the EvalValue type and all eval_* functions (eval_binary, eval_expression_in_context, eval_func_call, eval_method_call, eval_index, eval_field, is_truthy, eval_value_equals, unwrap_optional, etc.) into a dedicated crates/colony-exec/src/eval.rs module. Executor in lib.rs would shrink to its genuine responsibility: shell execution orchestration. The stdlib operation duplication between eval_func_call and eval_method_call can then be resolved by making the method form delegate to the function form.

issues.summary: eval_func_call in lib.rs contains literal duplicate match arms for 'trim' and 'replace', and mirrors eval_method_call arm-for-arm
evidence: Lines 946-951 (trim) and lines 1122-1127 (trim again) — identical implementations inside the same match statement in eval_func_call
Lines 953-967 (replace with 3 args) and lines 1129-1143 (replace again) — identical implementations, both mapped to the string 'replace'

eval_func_call and eval_method_call implement len, join, split, keys, values, get, has, upper, lower, trim, replace, contains, first, last, push, pop, insert, remove, slice independently with only the argument extraction pattern differing — method form uses 'target' instead of 'args[0]'
issues.suggestion: Collapse the duplicate arms inside eval_func_call (the second 'trim' and second 'replace' entries are unreachable dead code). Then refactor eval_method_call to extract the target value, prepend it to args, and delegate to eval_func_call for operations that are logically identical regardless of call style.

issues.summary: repl_tui.rs combines six distinct concerns in 1566 lines: ANSI stripping, pipe-based output capture, scrollback buffer, TUI rendering, keyboard/mouse dispatch, and command execution
evidence: strip_ansi() (lines 231-285): standalone text-processing utility with no dependency on the TUI state
OutputCapture (lines 152-226): an OS-level pipe/dup2/thread mechanism, a complete independent concern
Scrollback (lines 67-145): a pure data structure with scroll logic, completely separable from TUI rendering
The run_tui_repl function and its event loop handles keyboard events, mouse events, prompt rendering, command execution dispatch, and panel message routing all inline
is_colony_terminal() is defined identically in both repl.rs (line 29) and repl_tui.rs (line 42)
issues.suggestion: Extract Scrollback and OutputCapture into repl_tui/scrollback.rs and repl_tui/capture.rs. Move strip_ansi to a shared location (colony-tui or colony-exec/buffers where ANSI stripping already exists). Hoist is_colony_terminal() to a single shared location accessible from both REPLs.

issues.summary: tutorial/explain/constructs.rs is built but entirely suppressed with #[allow(dead_code)], suggesting an incomplete integration
evidence: Lines 5, 10, 24: #[allow(dead_code)] on ConceptExplainer, Concept, and the impl block — the module compiles but is not connected to any call site
The module is declared in the tutorial crate but the ConceptExplainer is not instantiated in tutorial/runner.rs or tutorial/tui/magic_pane.rs
issues.suggestion: Either wire ConceptExplainer into the magic pane (it appears the pane handles TraceEvent::Concept already via the Concept SectionStyle variant) or remove it until it is needed. Dead module-level code with suppressed warnings is a design signal that the feature was built speculatively.

issues.summary: McpConnection::reconnect leaves state=Reconnecting after a failed reconnect attempt
evidence: On reconnection failure (line 270-278) the code logs the error then sets self.state = ConnectionState::Reconnecting and returns Err(e).
ConnectionState::Reconnecting is documented as 'Connection was lost, attempting reconnect'; setting it after the attempt is done misrepresents the state.
Callers that inspect connection_state() after a failed reconnect will see Reconnecting and may retry prematurely or not surface the failure to the user.
issues.suggestion: Set self.state = ConnectionState::Disconnected (or introduce a new TransientFailure variant) after a failed reconnect attempt; only use Reconnecting while the attempt is in-flight.

issues.summary: GoalTree::add_blocker silently changes goal.status to Blocked without documenting the side-effect
evidence: Doc comment on add_blocker (line 151) says only 'Add a blocker to a goal'.
Implementation sets goal.status = GoalStatus::Blocked (line 158) and updates goal.updated_at.
A caller that calls add_blocker to record an advisory blocker without intending a status transition will have the goal's status changed under them.
issues.suggestion: Either update the doc comment to say 'Add a blocker and transition status to Blocked', or separate the concerns: add_note_blocker (pure append) vs. block_goal (changes status). At minimum the doc must state the status mutation.

issues.summary: BuiltinResult::is_success returns false for Source and Eval variants even though both represent exit code 0
evidence: is_success (line 48) only matches BuiltinResult::Success(0); Source(_, _) and Eval(_) are not matched.
exit_code() (line 38-46) returns 0 for both Source and Eval, making them semantically successful.
A caller checking is_success() after builtin_source or builtin_eval will incorrectly conclude the command failed even on a successful run.
issues.suggestion: Expand is_success to include Source and Eval with exit-code 0: `matches!(self, BuiltinResult::Success(0) | BuiltinResult::Source(_, _) | BuiltinResult::Eval(_))`, or add a sub-predicate is_zero_exit() that checks exit_code() == 0 and use that where appropriate.

issues.summary: McpConnectionPool::connect_all returns Ok(()) even when all auto-start servers fail to connect
evidence: All individual server failures are caught and logged (lines 84-90) but errors are swallowed.
After the loop, Ok(()) is returned unconditionally (line 100) regardless of how many connections were established.

If all servers fail, self.connections remains empty while the caller receives a success result, violating the implicit contract that Result<()> from a 'connect' operation means at least one connection is usable.
issues.suggestion: After the loop, if self.connections.is_empty() return Err(McpError::AllServersFailed) or a similar error. Alternatively document explicitly that Ok(()) means 'attempted, some may have failed, check all_tools() to see what is available'.

issues.summary: expand_arithmetic_immut silently discards assignment side-effects despite being named 'immutable'
evidence: The comment on expand_arithmetic_immut (line 26) says 'Immutable version for compatibility - creates a temporary mutable context'.
It clones the context, evaluates on the clone, then discards the clone; assignments like x++ in the arithmetic expression silently have no effect on the caller's context.
A caller who uses expand_arithmetic_immut for an expression like '++i' expecting idiomatic arithmetic evaluation will get the correct return value but i will not be incremented in their context.
issues.suggestion: Rename the function to expand_arithmetic_no_side_effects or expand_arithmetic_read_only and update the doc to state explicitly that variable assignments are not propagated. The current name 'immut' implies immutability of the function's output, not that it discards mutation of the input context.

issues.summary: C-style for loop body uses two sequential if-blocks that together mean 'break unless Normal', obscuring the single intended condition
evidence: Lines 252-257: `if !matches!(loop_flow, ControlFlow::Normal | ControlFlow::Continue) { break; }` followed immediately by `if matches!(loop_flow, ControlFlow::Continue) { break; }`. After the first check, loop_flow can only be Normal or Continue. The second check therefore fires exactly when Continue, making both together equivalent to `if loop_flow != ControlFlow::Normal { break; }`.
The intent (advance past continue-triggered iterations but break on Break/Exit/Return) is correct but requires two separate reasoning steps to verify.
issues.suggestion: Replace both if-blocks with a single check: `if !matches!(loop_flow, ControlFlow::Normal) { break; }`. This matches how the corresponding for-in loop handles the same cases (line 216-223 uses a match that is immediately understandable).

issues.summary: McpConnection::reconnect sets state to Reconnecting after a failed reconnect attempt instead of retaining the failure state
evidence: Lines 270-278: when self.connect() fails, the Err branch logs the error and then sets `self.state = ConnectionState::Reconnecting` (line 276) before returning Err. At the time of return the connection is not reconnecting — it has failed.
Callers observing the connection state after a failed reconnect will see Reconnecting, which implies an active background process, not a terminal failure for this attempt.

By contrast, the success path (line 264) correctly sets nothing (connect() already sets state=Connected internally). The failure path should either leave state as Disconnected (set by disconnect() called on line 260) or set it to Failed.
issues.suggestion: Remove the `self.state = ConnectionState::Reconnecting;` assignment from the Err branch (line 276). The state was already set to Disconnected by the preceding `self.disconnect().await` call, which is the accurate state after a failed reconnect attempt. If a persistent 'reconnect in progress' state is needed, that signal belongs at the pool level, not within the failed connection.

issues.summary: maybe_decrypt_value uses three-level nested conditionals where a combinator chain would be clearer
evidence: Lines 37-44: `if is_encrypted { if let Some(key) = get_cached_secure_key() { if let Ok(decrypted) = decrypt(..) { return decrypted; } } }`. Three levels of nesting for a try-decrypt-else-passthrough operation.
Project RUST_STYLE_GUIDE.md explicitly prohibits nested if-let: 'Nested if let is Always Wrong. If you write if let inside another if let, stop and refactor.'
The decryption check can be expressed as a combinator: `is_encrypted(&value).then(|| get_cached_secure_key()?.and_then(|key| decrypt(&value, key).ok())).flatten().unwrap_or(value)` or via let-else.
issues.suggestion: Flatten using let-else: `if !colony_secure::is_encrypted(&value) { return value; }; let Some(key) = get_cached_secure_key() else { return value; }; colony_secure::decrypt(&value, key).unwrap_or(value)`. This makes each guard a single exit point and matches the project's stated style.

issues.summary: get_var_or_env_raw NameRef branch uses a four-level nested if-let pyramid in violation of project style guide
evidence: Lines 1176-1184: `if let Some(var) = self.variables.get(name) { if let Variable::NameRef(_target) = var { if let Some(resolved) = self.resolve_nameref(name) { if let Some(target_var) = self.variables.get(&resolved) { return ...; } return ...; } return None; } return ...; }`. Four nesting levels.
The same NameRef resolution logic appears in get_variable (lines 1007-1013) and set_variable (lines 1256-1261) using a more direct pattern. The get_var_or_env_raw version is the most convoluted.
Project style guide: 'No exceptions. If you think you need nested if let, you don't.'
issues.suggestion: Refactor using let-else at each decision point: `let Some(var) = self.variables.get(name) else { return self.environment.get(name).cloned(); }; if !matches!(var, Variable::NameRef(_)) { return Some(var.as_str().to_string()); }; let Some(resolved) = self.resolve_nameref(name) else { return None; }; if let Some(target_var) = self.variables.get(&resolved) { return Some(target_var.as_str().to_string()); }; return self.environment.get(&resolved).cloned();`

issues.summary: Timestamp fields typed as String carry ISO-8601 semantic contracts not enforced by the type
evidence: InstalledRecipe::installed_at: String (registry.rs:20) — populated by callers with RFC-3339 strings but nothing prevents arbitrary non-date strings
Goal::created_at: String, updated_at: String (goals/types.rs:53-55) — set via chrono::Utc::now().to_rfc3339() but stored and compared as bare strings throughout the tree
issues.suggestion: Replace String timestamp fields with chrono::DateTime<Utc>; serde's built-in support handles serialization. This makes the contract machine-verifiable and eliminates silent format mismatches.

issues.summary: GoalTree::storage_path panics instead of returning Result when home directory is missing
evidence: tree.rs:72-76: dirs::home_dir().expect("home directory must exist") inside the private storage_path helper — this is called from the public GoalTree::load which returns Result<Self>, so the error contract is broken before the ? operator can propagate it
issues.suggestion: Change storage_path to return Result<PathBuf, GoalError> and propagate the missing-home-dir case as GoalError::InvalidOperation, allowing callers to handle it rather than crashing.

issues.summary: McpToolInfo in colony-recipe and ToolInfo in colony-mcp are parallel type definitions for the same concept
evidence: McpToolInfo (mcp_lifecycle.rs:33-37): name: String, description: Option<String>, server_name: String
ToolInfo (connection.rs:56-61): tool: Tool (rmcp type embedding name/description), server_name: String
Any cross-subsystem code that needs both shapes must manually map between them, and the shapes can diverge silently
issues.suggestion: Either unify into a single canonical ToolInfo in a shared crate (colony-config or a new colony-mcp-types), or make McpToolInfo a view over ToolInfo. The divergence risks future schema drift.

issues.summary: SidebarConfig panel lists use Vec<String> where a PanelId newtype or enum would enforce validity
evidence: SidebarConfig::panels: Vec<String> and collapsed_panels: Vec<String> (manager.rs:15-16) are populated with literal panel names like "file_tree", "session", "mcp", "git_files"
The SidebarManager::on_event method matches against subscribed strings (manager.rs:158-165), creating a stringly-typed event dispatch
A typo in a panel name string silently produces a missing panel rather than a compile-time error
issues.suggestion: Define a PanelId enum with all known panel variants, or at minimum a newtype wrapper with an exhaustive from_str. This would surface panel name mismatches at compile time or at startup rather than silently.

issues.summary: control_flow.rs test module only checks enum variant count, not any behavioral logic
evidence: The sole test in control_flow.rs is: let values = [ControlFlow::Normal, ControlFlow::Break, ControlFlow::Continue, ControlFlow::Exit, ControlFlow::Return]; assert_eq!(values.len(), 5);
execute_list_with_control, execute_statement_with_control, the break/continue/return propagation through nested loops, and the exit trap invocation are all untested
issues.suggestion: Replace with behavioral tests using exec_program from colony-exec's test helpers: verify that `for i in 1 2 3; do break; done` exits after one iteration, that `continue` skips the remainder of the loop body, and that `return` inside a function propagates the code back to the caller.

issues.summary: Shell execution entry points engine.rs and orchestrator.rs have zero tests
evidence: grep for #[cfg(test)] in engine.rs, orchestrator.rs, and repl.rs returns no matches

execute_command_with_status (the -c flag entry point) and execute_shell_command (the REPL entry point) contain parsing, trap execution, and exit-code handling that is tested only indirectly through the bats suite
issues.suggestion: Add unit tests for execute_command_with_status that create a bare Executor, call the function with shell strings, and assert the returned exit code. The function is synchronous-friendly enough for tokio::test blocks. At minimum cover: successful command returns 0, parse error returns 2, exit trap runs on exit.

issues.summary: colony-mcp connection and pool modules have zero unit tests
evidence: grep for #[cfg(test)] in crates/colony-mcp/src/connection.rs returns no matches
grep for #[cfg(test)] in crates/colony-mcp/src/pool.rs returns no matches
ConnectionState transitions, ToolInfo caching, pool routing logic (all_tools(), call_tool() routing) are completely untested at the unit level
issues.suggestion: Add unit tests for ConnectionState transitions (Disconnected→Connected→Reconnecting→Failed state machine) using direct struct construction. For McpConnectionPool, test call_tool routing with a mock McpConnection that records which server received the call — or at minimum test the error path when no server provides the requested tool.

issues.summary: Redirect tests use hardcoded /tmp paths causing parallel-run and ordering fragility
evidence: test_output_redirect writes to /tmp/colony_test_output.txt
test_append_redirect writes to /tmp/colony_test_append.txt
test_fd_duplication writes to /tmp/colony_test_fd_dup.txt
test_heredoc_no_expand writes to /tmp/colony_heredoc_no_expand.txt
All tests use fs::remove_file before and after but without mutual exclusion; concurrent cargo test runs will collide
issues.suggestion: Replace all hardcoded /tmp paths with tempfile::NamedTempFile or tempfile::tempdir(), which are already used elsewhere in the test suite (e.g., colony-exec/src/mirror.rs). This eliminates collision risk entirely.

issues.summary: background.rs and serialization.rs contain placeholder-quality tests that assert constants or a single trivial case
evidence: background.rs sole test: assert_eq!(MAX_JOBS, 128) — does not test run_in_background
serialization.rs sole test: round-trips 'echo hello' through statement_to_shell_string — no coverage of SingleQuoted, DoubleQuoted with variables, pipeline serialization, or redirect serialization
issues.suggestion: For serialization.rs, add tests for: single-quoted strings with special characters, double-quoted strings containing $VAR references, and pipelines with multiple commands. For background.rs, add a test that calls run_in_background with a trivial statement (e.g., sleep 0) and verifies a JobId and Pid are returned.

issues.summary: No Rust-level integration test connects the agent → tool execution → expansion chain
evidence: Only one external integration test file exists (colony-reflection/tests/integration.rs) covering the observation lifecycle
The agent.rs tests cover only pure config defaults and model inference, not process() or process_full() which involve the provider, tool registry, approval, and conversation store
The interaction between tool execution, cancellation, and persistence is exercised only in production
issues.suggestion: Add a colony-agent integration test that creates an Agent with a mock provider returning a fixed StreamEvent sequence, calls process(), and asserts the response text, message count, and (if persistence is enabled) that the conversation store contains the expected messages.

issues.summary: colony-exec absorbs 8 subsystems (file_tree, flux, goals, mirror, panes, sidebar, buffers, special_files) unrelated to its stated fork/exec responsibility
evidence: lib.rs docstring: 'Command execution with fork/exec and job control ... Simple command execution, PATH resolution, Environment passing, Exit status capture' — does not mention the 8 public submodules that are unrelated to these primitives.
pub mod file_tree, flux, goals, mirror, panes, sidebar, buffers, special_files are all publicly exported from a crate documented as an execution engine.

builtins.rs dispatch (lines 271-296) routes 'tree', 'split', 'vsplit', 'layout', 'pane', 'mirror', 'goal' builtins to colony-exec internal submodules — forcing all feature builtins to live inside the execution crate.
colony-exec/src/ has 19,239 total LOC; for comparison, colony-parser (the entire POSIX parser) is 7,962 LOC — exec has become a superset of the whole codebase.
issues.suggestion: Extract each distinct subsystem into its own crate or at minimum into colony-shell: colony-exec/src/mirror.rs -> colony-mirror or colony-shell/src/shell/mirror; colony-exec/src/goals/ -> use colony-focus directly; colony-exec/src/flux/ -> colony-flux or colony-shell/src/shell/flux; colony-exec/src/panes/ -> already has colony-panel, move logic there; colony-exec/src/file_tree/ -> already has colony-filetree, remove duplication; colony-exec/src/special_files/ -> colony-shell/src/shell/special_files (it reads AGENT.md, CONTEXT.md — shell startup logic, not exec primitives). Update builtins.rs to call into those crates at dispatch time. Update lib.rs docstring to match whatever remains.

issues.summary: colony-ui-core exports two competing file-tree implementations: one with inline std::fs walking and one using colony-filetree::TreeState
evidence: builtins/sidebar_file_tree.rs (FileTreeSidebarComponent): uses std::fs::read_dir in walk_directory() with its own max_depth/max_entries limits — an inline re-implementation of file tree traversal.
sidebar/panels/file_tree.rs (FileTreePanel): uses colony_filetree::TreeState::new(root) — the proper shared library.

lib.rs line 26: pub use builtins::FileTreeSidebarComponent and lib.rs line 39: pub use sidebar::FileTreePanel — both are exported at crate root, both represent 'the file tree sidebar', with no documentation explaining which to prefer or why both exist.
issues.suggestion: Remove the inline std::fs walking in FileTreeSidebarComponent and have it delegate to colony-filetree::TreeState (same as FileTreePanel does), or consolidate both types into one. If FileTreeSidebarComponent implements PromptComponent and FileTreePanel implements SidebarComponent (different traits), document this distinction and remove the inline fs traversal from FileTreeSidebarComponent, replacing it with colony_filetree.

issues.summary: DockerStatusComponent calls docker CLI synchronously at render time instead of subscribing to tuple-space events, breaking the reactive component architecture
evidence: get_running_count() calls Command::new('docker').args(['ps', '-q']).output() on every render() invocation — a blocking subprocess call inside the render path.
subscriptions() returns vec![] — this component declares no reactive dependencies, so the rendering engine has no mechanism to know when Docker state changes without calling render repeatedly.
All other seed-file components (aws_profile, duration) read from ComponentContext (pre-computed, side-effect-free) — DockerStatus is the only component that spawns a process during render.
If docker is not installed or the daemon is not running, render silently returns hidden — the component architecture has no contract for this failure mode.
issues.suggestion: Either: (1) add a Docker-monitoring tuple emitter (separate background task that polls docker and emits docker_status tuples to the tuple space), then update DockerStatusComponent.subscriptions() to subscribe to those tuples and read count from ComponentContext.data, matching the pattern of other components; or (2) cache the subprocess result with a TTL and document the divergence from the reactive contract. Option 1 keeps the architecture coherent.

issues.summary: Persistence stores split between sync open() and async open() with no naming convention to signal which applies
evidence: ConversationStore::open, GoalStore::open, ObservationStore::open, and ApprovalDatabase::open are all synchronous
MemoryStore::open, PersistentTupleSpace::open, colony-tuple ipc::TupleIpc::open are all async
No naming distinguishes these families — both groups are called 'open' with no 'async_open', 'open_async', or 'connect' prefix to warn callers
A developer wiring three stores into an init function must inspect each implementation to know whether .await is required
issues.suggestion: Establish and document a crate-level convention: synchronous stores keep open(), async stores use async fn open() but also provide a synchronous blocking::open() that wraps spawn_blocking, or alternatively rename async openers to connect() or open_async() to make the contract visible at the call site.

issues.summary: Agent::process() and Agent::process_full() are two public entry points with invisible behavioural difference: tool call handling
evidence: process() at line 353 builds a completion stream, wraps it in cancellable_stream, and collects text — tool events in the stream are silently dropped by the StreamEvent::_ arm in cancellable_stream
process_full() at line 476 performs explicit stream polling including StreamEvent::ToolCallStart and StreamEvent::ToolCallComplete dispatch to handle_tool_use()
The name 'full' communicates the difference only loosely; there is no type-level distinction (both return Result<String>) and no doc comment on process() warning that tool calls are not executed
A caller choosing process() for an agent configured with tools will silently receive no tool execution
issues.suggestion: Either merge into a single process() that always handles tool calls (making tool handling the default, not opt-in), or introduce a type-level distinction such as returning a ProcessHandle enum so callers cannot accidentally choose the wrong mode. At minimum, add a doc comment on process() that explicitly states tool calls are ignored.

issues.summary: OllamaProvider::supports_streaming() returns true but the implementation sends stream:false and emits a single synthetic event
evidence: supports_streaming() at line 150 returns true with comment 'Ollama supports streaming via newline-delimited JSON'
complete() at line 85 sets stream: Some(false) in OllamaRequest at line 104 with comment '// Non-streaming for initial implementation'
The response is a single OllamaResponse struct parsed as JSON, then wrapped in two fake stream events (TextDelta + Done) at lines 142-145
A downstream consumer relying on supports_streaming() to choose a rendering strategy will receive batch behaviour despite the declared capability
issues.suggestion: Either implement real Ollama NDJSON streaming (iterate the streaming API) or change supports_streaming() to return false until the implementation is complete. The comment 'Ollama supports streaming' is correct about the server capability but misrepresents the current client implementation.

issues.summary: OllamaProvider::is_available() duplicates a subset of health_check() as a separate async bool method not part of the trait
evidence: is_available() at line 48 performs an HTTP GET /api/tags and returns bool
health_check() at line 168 also starts with an HTTP GET /api/tags and additionally checks model availability
is_available() is not part of the ModelProvider trait and thus not available through trait objects — it can only be called on concrete OllamaProvider
Callers have two paths: one that returns a structured ProviderHealth (with latency, error detail) and one that returns a bare bool from essentially the same request
issues.suggestion: Remove is_available() from the public surface and make health_check() the single availability oracle. If callers need a quick bool, they can check health_check().available. Alternatively, promote is_available to the ModelProvider trait if fast bool checks are needed across all providers.

issues.summary: Sibling persistence stores accept either &Path or impl Into<PathBuf> for the path parameter with no consistent rule
evidence: ConversationStore::open takes impl Into<PathBuf> (line 42 in persistence.rs)
GoalStore::open takes impl Into<PathBuf> (line 22 in focus/persistence.rs)
ApprovalDatabase::open takes &Path (line 28 in approvals.rs)
ObservationStore::open takes &Path (line 46 in storage.rs)
Both forms are valid Rust, but the inconsistency adds cognitive overhead when wiring stores — a developer must check each open() signature to know whether to pass path.as_path() or just path
issues.suggestion: Standardize on impl AsRef<Path> across all persistence stores, which accepts both &Path and &PathBuf without requiring the caller to convert, and is more general than impl Into<PathBuf>.

issues.summary: Agent::new(), with_config(), and with_provider() duplicate the same struct initialization block, inflating the API with three async constructors
evidence: new() at line 104 calls with_config(AgentConfig::default())
with_config() at lines 186-222 builds router, tools, approval, token_tracker, context_manager and returns Self
with_provider() at lines 225-269 builds router differently but repeats the identical tools/approval/token_tracker/context_manager initialization verbatim
Any change to the initialization logic (e.g. adding a new field) must be applied in two places
issues.suggestion: Extract a private new_from_router(router, config) constructor used by both with_config() and with_provider(), eliminating the duplicated initialization block. This also makes future fields added to Agent easier to maintain.

issues.summary: Two parallel sidebar panel implementations coexist under builtins/ and sidebar/panels/ with different type names and line types
evidence: FileTreeSidebarComponent in builtins/sidebar_file_tree.rs and FileTreePanel in sidebar/panels/file_tree.rs both implement SidebarComponent for the same 'file_tree' id, but use different line types (SidebarLine vs ComponentLine) and different class-name suffixes.

GitFilesSidebarComponent in builtins/sidebar_git_files.rs and GitFilesPanel in sidebar/panels/git_files.rs both parse git porcelain output and render git file lists independently, with diverging status type enums (GitFileStatus defined in both files with different variant sets: panels version has Staged/Conflict variants the builtins version lacks).
McpSidebarComponent and McpPanel, SessionSidebarComponent and SessionPanel: four pairs of structurally equivalent components across two directories.
issues.suggestion: Determine which implementation is canonical and delete the other. The builtins/ variants use SidebarLine (which has a From<SidebarLine> for ComponentLine conversion already defined) and appear more featureful; the sidebar/panels/ variants use ComponentLine directly. Pick one set, update all callers, and remove the duplicate directory. Do not add an abstraction layer to unify them — simply pick the richer implementation.

issues.summary: colony-filetree-bin subscribes to 'cwd_change' but the system emits 'dir_change'; the binary silently never reacts to directory changes
evidence: colony-filetree-bin/src/main.rs line 24: `subscriptions: vec!["cwd_change".to_string()]`
colony-filetree-bin/src/main.rs line 65: `if key == "cwd_change"`
colony-exec/src/builtins.rs lines 369, 4239, 4280, 4317, 4395, 6735: all emit `Value::Str("dir_change".to_string())` as the tuple key for directory change events

colony-shell/src/repl_tui.rs line 830: the TUI host broadcasts key 'cwd_change' to panels specifically — this is a separate panel-protocol broadcast path. The tuple-space path uses 'dir_change'. The subscription to 'cwd_change' may be intentional for the panel host path, but the comment on line 63 of filetree-bin reads '// React to dir_change' while the code checks 'cwd_change', indicating at minimum a documentation/convention inconsistency.
issues.suggestion: Audit whether colony-filetree-bin is intended to receive events via the panel-host broadcast path (which does use 'cwd_change') or via the tuple space (which uses 'dir_change'). If panel-host broadcast is the intended path, fix the comment on line 63 to say 'cwd_change'. If tuple space is intended, change the subscription key and matching key from 'cwd_change' to 'dir_change'. Add a constant (e.g. `const KEY_DIR_CHANGE: &str = "dir_change"`) shared across the panel binaries to prevent this class of mismatch.

issues.summary: Sibling panel binaries use different error handling style: colony-env-bin uses .expect() with messages, colony-filetree-bin uses bare .unwrap()
evidence: colony-env-bin/src/main.rs line 25: `serde_json::to_string(&config).expect("config must serialize")`
colony-env-bin/src/main.rs line 111: `serde_json::to_string(&line).expect("frame line must serialize")`
colony-filetree-bin/src/main.rs line 35: `serde_json::to_string(&config).unwrap()` — bare unwrap, no message
colony-filetree-bin/src/main.rs lines 105, 118: two more bare `.unwrap()` on serialization calls that env-bin treats with .expect()
issues.suggestion: Replace the three bare `.unwrap()` calls in colony-filetree-bin/src/main.rs with `.expect("<msg>")` matching the convention established in colony-env-bin: `serde_json::to_string(&config).expect("config must serialize")`, `serde_json::to_string(&line).expect("frame line must serialize")`, `serde_json::to_string(&emit).expect("tuple emit must serialize")`.

issues.summary: File extension-to-icon mapping is implemented three times independently with diverging extension sets and icon codepoints
evidence: colony-filetree-bin/src/main.rs defines `fn file_icon(name: &str) -> &'static str` covering rs/toml/json/yaml/md/txt/sh/bash/zsh/py/js/ts/go/c/cpp/h

colony-ui-core/src/builtins/sidebar_file_tree.rs defines `fn file_icon(name: &str) -> (&'static str, Color)` covering rs/toml/md/json/js/ts/py/go/sh/bash/zsh/lock/yml/yaml — different icon codepoints for the same extensions, adds Color

colony-ui-core/src/sidebar/panels/file_tree.rs defines `fn file_style(&self, ext: &Option<String>) -> (&'static str, Color)` covering rs/toml/json/yaml/yml/md/txt/sh/bash/zsh/py/js/ts/jsx/tsx/go/c/cpp/h/hpp/html/htm/css/scss/sass/lock — the most complete set, but different codepoints for the same extensions vs the builtins version
issues.suggestion: If the sidebar_dual_implementation issue is resolved by picking one set of sidebar components, two of these three will naturally be removed. If the panel binary is also updated to use the ui-core library's mapping, only one copy needs to exist. Short of that, move the mapping into a shared function in a crate that both the binary and the ui-core library can depend on (e.g., a small file in colony-panel or a new colony-icons helper). Do not add a dependency inversion layer — a simple `pub fn file_icon(ext: &str) -> (&'static str, Color)` in the right shared crate is sufficient.

issues.summary: Silent timestamp substitution on invalid RFC3339 data masks corrupt approval records
evidence: Lines 162-164 and 204-206: DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(&granted_at_str).map(|dt| dt.with_timezone(&Utc)).unwrap_or_else(|_| Utc::now()) — a parse failure silently substitutes the current time
This pattern appears identically in both list_approvals() and list_all_approvals()
In a security-audit context (approval records for sensitive variable access), silently replacing a corrupt timestamp with the current time produces misleading results with no diagnostic
issues.suggestion: Propagate the parse error instead: use DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(&granted_at_str).map_err(|e| rusqlite::Error::FromSqlConversionFailure(4, rusqlite::types::Type::Text, Box::new(e)))? inside the query_map closure, or define a SecureError variant for database integrity failures and use map_err(|_| SecureError::CorruptTimestamp(granted_at_str.clone())). At minimum, log a warning with the raw value before substituting.

issues.summary: TreeState::load() failure in get_tree_state() is silently discarded with no log or error propagation
evidence: Lines 50-55: 'if new_state.load().is_ok()' — the Err variant is discarded with no tracing::warn! or debug! call
The fallback path (lines 204-217) renders '(failed to load)' in the UI, but the underlying error reason is never recorded
Contrast: handle_action() on line 230 uses tracing::debug! for toggle events — the tracing infrastructure is available and used elsewhere in this file
issues.suggestion: Replace 'if new_state.load().is_ok()' with 'match new_state.load() { Ok(()) => { ... } Err(e) => { tracing::warn!("FileTreePanel: failed to load tree for {}: {}", root.display(), e); } }' to record why the tree failed to load while preserving the existing graceful-degradation UI behavior.

issues.summary: Sibling panel binaries treat serde_json serialization panics inconsistently: unwrap() vs expect("msg")
evidence: colony-filetree-bin line 35: serde_json::to_string(&config).unwrap() — no message on panic
colony-filetree-bin lines 105, 118: serde_json::to_string(&line).unwrap() and serde_json::to_string(&emit).unwrap()
colony-env-bin line 25: serde_json::to_string(&config).expect("config must serialize") — has context message
colony-env-bin line 111: serde_json::to_string(&line).expect("frame line must serialize") — has context message
Both binaries implement the same panel protocol pattern; one has diagnostic context, the other does not
issues.suggestion: Apply the colony-env-bin pattern to colony-filetree-bin: replace each .unwrap() with a matching .expect("<what> must serialize") call. E.g., serde_json::to_string(&config).expect("PanelConfig must serialize"), serde_json::to_string(&line).expect("FrameLine must serialize"), serde_json::to_string(&emit).expect("TupleEmit must serialize").

issues.summary: get_tree_state mutates internal state via RwLock writes behind a get_ prefix
evidence: fn get_tree_state(&self, root: &Path) -> Option<TreeState> acquires self.current_root.write() and self.tree_state.write() and conditionally overwrites both (lines 40-58)
Rust convention: get_ methods are expected to be read-only accessors; callers of &self methods do not expect mutation
issues.suggestion: Rename to ensure_tree_state or load_or_init_tree_state to signal that it may initialize on first call or when the root changes

issues.summary: setup_notification_channel always returns Ok(None) — name promises initialization that never happens
evidence: fn setup_notification_channel(_config: &IpcConfig) -> Result<Option<IpcSender<TupleNotification>>> { Ok(None) } with comment 'For phase 1: Just create a channel but don't connect yet' (lines 253-259)
The name 'setup' implies the channel is created/registered; callers cannot distinguish 'disabled by config' from 'not yet implemented'
issues.suggestion: Either rename to placeholder_notification_channel or, better, inline the phase-1 stub at the call site in IpcTupleSpace::open with a TODO comment so the unused function does not mislead future readers

issues.summary: process_full / process_with_cancellation pair uses 'full' as a negative qualifier rather than describing what the method does
evidence: pub async fn process_with_cancellation(...) at line 359 is the primary method with explicit cancel token
pub async fn process_full(...) at line 476 handles the streaming/tool-call path — 'full' contrasts with 'with_cancellation' but does not describe the streaming behavior
A reader must read both bodies to understand that process_full is the streaming tool-use path
issues.suggestion: Rename process_full to run_turn or execute_turn to name what it does, and consider whether process_with_cancellation should be the primary public API; the current naming makes the streaming path look like an enhanced version rather than a distinct code path

issues.summary: process_widget_message uses generic 'process' verb at a dispatch boundary
evidence: async fn process_widget_message(json: &str, ...) -> Option<String> at line 193 parses JSON, matches on ProtocolMessage variants, and routes to typed handlers
The function is purely a dispatcher — callers already know a message is being processed; the name adds no information about what happens to the message
issues.suggestion: Rename to dispatch_widget_message or route_widget_request to communicate the routing/dispatch nature of the function

issues.summary: ShoptOptions.get() and .set() implement string-keyed dispatch over struct fields that are already typeable by name
evidence: ShoptOptions::get(name: &str) -> Option<bool> contains a 25-arm match that maps string literals to struct field reads; the caller already knows the field by name at compile time in almost all call sites
ShoptOptions::set(name: &str, value: bool) -> bool is a parallel 25-arm match for writes; any typo or missing case is a silent None/false rather than a compile error

The only justification for string-keyed access is the shopt builtin which receives runtime strings from user input — that specific call site could receive the dispatch while all internal callers use direct field access
issues.suggestion: Keep the string dispatch methods only for the shopt builtin handler that receives runtime user strings. All internal callers that currently pass a string literal should access the struct fields directly (e.g., context.shopt.extglob instead of context.shopt.get("extglob")). This eliminates the runtime dispatch overhead and makes typos compile errors.

issues.summary: ProtocolEmitter is a zero-field struct whose two methods provide no protocol abstraction over raw stdout/debug
evidence: ProtocolEmitter is defined as `pub struct ProtocolEmitter {}` with no fields
emit_thought() calls print!() then flush() — the caller could do this directly
emit_tool_call() calls debug!() and returns Ok(()) — effectively a no-op wrapper over a logging call
The comment '// Emits OSC 2337 sequences for colony-terminal' suggests intended future behavior that was never implemented, leaving a placeholder abstraction in place
issues.suggestion: Either remove ProtocolEmitter and have Agent call stdout/tracing directly for the two call sites, or implement the OSC 2337 protocol it promises and make the abstraction earn its keep. As-is, it costs an indirection level for zero behavioral value.

issues.summary: RecipeAgentConfig.merge_with_overrides() and apply_recipe_to_config() both translate Recipe fields to AgentConfig fields with nearly identical logic
evidence: merge_with_overrides() builds an AgentConfig by first copying recipe values then overriding with user values — a two-pass field copy

apply_recipe_to_config() also copies recipe.prompt.system, recipe.model.temperature, and recipe.tools.approval.auto_approve into an existing AgentConfig — the same three fields, the same conditional logic
Both functions exist in the same module and handle the same translation domain; callers must decide which path to use without a clear protocol boundary
issues.suggestion: Consolidate to a single translation function. apply_recipe_to_config is the simpler form (in-place mutation); merge_with_overrides can call it internally, then apply overrides on top. This collapses two nearly-identical translation paths into one and makes the override semantics explicit rather than duplicated.

issues.summary: AgentTupleBridge.space() and .subscriptions() return references to inner types, making the wrapper leaky
evidence: space() -> &TupleSpace returns a plain reference to the inner TupleSpace; callers can call any TupleSpace method directly, bypassing the bridge's subscription notification logic
subscriptions() -> &SubscriptionManager similarly exposes the raw manager

write_tuple() and write_tool_result() both call self.space.out() AND self.subscriptions.notify() together — the bridge's value is that it keeps these two calls in sync; the accessors allow callers to call space.out() without notify(), breaking the invariant
issues.suggestion: Remove space() and subscriptions() from the public API or make them crate-private. Callers that need to read from the tuple space should use a dedicated read method on the bridge itself. If external callers genuinely need the full TupleSpace API, consider whether the bridge abstraction is appropriate at all.

issues.summary: MemoryIntegration.is_enabled() and .config() are single-field accessors over a private config struct
evidence: is_enabled() returns self.config.enabled — a one-liner that adds one indirection level for no policy
config() -> &MemoryConfig returns &self.config — a raw reference to the full config struct, exposing all config fields to callers anyway
If config() is public, callers can check config().enabled directly, making is_enabled() redundant
issues.suggestion: Remove is_enabled(); callers that already receive a &MemoryIntegration reference can call .config().enabled if needed, or check before constructing. Alternatively make the config field pub directly on MemoryIntegration since config() already exposes it.

issues.summary: signal-hook-tokio declared in workspace.dependencies but never used by any crate
evidence: `signal-hook-tokio = { version = "0.3", features = ["futures-v0_3"] }` appears in Cargo.toml [workspace.dependencies] at line 58
Grep across all crates/*/Cargo.toml and src/ finds zero references to signal-hook-tokio or signal_hook_tokio
issues.suggestion: Remove the `signal-hook-tokio` entry from [workspace.dependencies] in the root Cargo.toml; if async signal handling is needed in the future, add it at that point.

issues.summary: rmp-serde (MessagePack) declared in workspace.dependencies but never used by any crate
evidence: `rmp-serde = "1.1"` appears in Cargo.toml [workspace.dependencies]
Grep across all crates/*/Cargo.toml and src/ finds zero references to rmp-serde or rmp_serde
issues.suggestion: Remove the `rmp-serde` entry from [workspace.dependencies]; if MessagePack serialization is added in the future, add it then.

issues.summary: colony-shell declares both terminal_size and term_size for the same purpose; term_size is unused
evidence: crates/colony-shell/Cargo.toml line 79: `terminal_size = "0.4"`
crates/colony-shell/Cargo.toml line 87: `term_size = "0.3"`
Only `terminal_size::terminal_size()` appears in source (repl.rs:290); `term_size` is never imported
issues.suggestion: Remove `term_size = "0.3"` from crates/colony-shell/Cargo.toml; the crate already uses `terminal_size = "0.4"` for all terminal dimension queries.

issues.summary: tera (full Jinja2 template engine) pulled into colony-mcp for a single 60-line TypeScript codegen file
evidence: crates/colony-mcp/Cargo.toml: `tera = "1"` is the only non-trivial template dependency
tera is used only in codegen.rs via `use tera::{Context, Tera}` to render a single static TypeScript template string defined as a `const` in the same file
The template has 6 interpolated variables (server_name, schema_hash, timestamp, tool fields) and a simple for-loop — no filters, inheritance, or macros beyond `default()`
tera transitively brings in pest, pest_derive, globset, humansize, and ~12 other crates
issues.suggestion: Replace `tera` with a simple hand-written string builder using `format!` and iterator chains; the template's logic is a for-loop over tools with string substitution, which does not justify a full template engine.

issues.summary: colony-expand declares both rand and getrandom; getrandom is redundant since rand provides OsRng
evidence: crates/colony-expand/Cargo.toml: `rand = "0.8"` and `getrandom = "0.2"` both listed
context.rs:17-18: `use rand::rngs::StdRng; use rand::{Rng, SeedableRng};` for $RANDOM
context.rs:1213: `getrandom::getrandom(&mut buf)` for $SRANDOM — this can be replaced with `rand::rngs::OsRng.fill_bytes(&mut buf)` which is provided by the already-present rand crate
issues.suggestion: Remove `getrandom = "0.2"` from crates/colony-expand/Cargo.toml and replace the `getrandom::getrandom()` call in context.rs with `rand::rngs::OsRng.fill_bytes(&mut buf)` (OsRng is re-exported from rand).

issues.summary: rusqlite with bundled SQLite declared independently in 6 crates instead of workspace, risking version drift
evidence: All six crates pin `rusqlite = { version = "0.32", features = ["bundled"] }` independently
`rusqlite` is absent from [workspace.dependencies] in root Cargo.toml, unlike tokio, serde, thiserror etc.
The `bundled` feature compiles SQLite from C source; having it duplicated across 6 Cargo.tomls rather than workspace makes it easy for one crate to drift to 0.33+ while others remain at 0.32
issues.suggestion: Add `rusqlite = { version = "0.32", features = ["bundled"] }` to [workspace.dependencies] in root Cargo.toml, then replace the 6 per-crate declarations with `rusqlite.workspace = true`.

issues.summary: colony-exec and colony-filetree configure notify with incompatible feature sets; colony-filetree's default-features=false optimization is negated
evidence: crates/colony-exec/Cargo.toml: `notify = "6"` (default features enabled, picks up inotify/kqueue/ReadDirectoryChanges backends)
crates/colony-filetree/Cargo.toml: `notify = { version = "6.1", default-features = false, features = ["macos_fsevent"] }` — explicitly opts out of non-macOS backends
In any binary that links both crates (e.g., the main colony shell), Cargo's feature resolver unions both sets, activating default features regardless of colony-filetree's intent
issues.suggestion: Align both crates to the same notify feature set. If the project targets macOS primarily, change colony-exec to also use `default-features = false, features = ["macos_fsevent"]`. Otherwise, promote `notify` to [workspace.dependencies] with explicit features and have both crates reference `notify.workspace = true`.

issues.summary: chrono and uuid declared per-crate 8 times each with minor version variations instead of workspace deps
evidence: uuid declared in 8 crates with three distinct pinned versions: `"1"`, `"1.6"`, and `"1.10"` — Cargo resolves to a common semver-compatible version but different minimum constraints mean independent upgrade decisions
colony-exec uses `chrono = "0.4"` (without serde feature) while the 7 other crates use `chrono = { version = "0.4", features = ["serde"] }` — inconsistent feature sets
Neither chrono nor uuid appears in [workspace.dependencies] despite tokio, serde, thiserror, tracing all being properly centralized there
issues.suggestion: Add `uuid = { version = "1.10", features = ["v4"] }` and `chrono = { version = "0.4", features = ["serde"] }` to [workspace.dependencies], then replace all per-crate declarations with `.workspace = true`. Update colony-exec's chrono usage to include serde or suppress the feature there explicitly.

issues.summary: Identical errexit error-handling blocks copy-pasted across 5+ match arms in execute_statement_with_errexit_control
evidence: The pattern 'match result { Ok(code) => if !errexit_exempt && errexit && code != 0 { Exit } else { Normal }, Err(Exit(c)) => Exit, Err(Errexit(c)) => Exit, Err(ref e) => { eprintln!; let exit_code = match e { CommandNotFound => 127, PermissionDenied => 126, _ => 1 }; if !errexit_exempt && errexit { Exit } else { Normal } }' appears essentially verbatim for SimpleCommand, Try, Match, While/Until/Case arms.
The execute_err_trap call is also repeated identically after the result for SimpleCommand, Try, Match, and Pipeline.
issues.suggestion: Extract a helper fn map_execution_result(result: Result<i32, ExecutionError>, errexit_exempt: bool, errexit: bool) -> (i32, ControlFlow) that encodes the common mapping. Each arm then becomes a one-liner that calls map_execution_result after await. The err_trap call can similarly be factored via a post-hook pattern.

issues.summary: ShoptOptions names listed three times independently in get(), set(), and all_options()
evidence: ShoptOptions::get() is a 25-arm match over string literals returning the corresponding field.
ShoptOptions::set() is a parallel 25-arm match assigning the same field.
ShoptOptions::all_options() returns a static slice listing the same 24 names alphabetically.
Any new shopt option requires three coordinated edits that are easy to miss.
issues.suggestion: Define a const array of (name, getter-closure, setter-closure) or use a macro to generate get/set/all_options from a single authoritative list. Alternatively, a phf::Map from name to field offset, or even just an index into a fixed-size array if all options are bool, would reduce the maintenance surface to one place.

issues.summary: maybe_decrypt_value() uses nested if-let pyramid in direct violation of the project style guide
evidence: Lines 37-44: 'if colony_secure::is_encrypted(&value) { if let Some(key) = get_cached_secure_key() { if let Ok(decrypted) = colony_secure::decrypt(&value, key) { return decrypted; } } }' — three levels of nesting.
RUST_STYLE_GUIDE.md states 'Nested if let is Always Wrong' with no exceptions.
issues.suggestion: Rewrite using let-else: 'let Some(key) = get_cached_secure_key() else { return value }; let Ok(decrypted) = colony_secure::decrypt(&value, key) else { return value }; decrypted' — or as a combinator chain on Option/Result.

issues.summary: execute_cstyle_for_loop_with_control breaks on Continue twice in succession — one break is unreachable
evidence: Lines 252-256: 'if !matches!(loop_flow, Normal | Continue) { break; } if matches!(loop_flow, Continue) { break; }' — when loop_flow is Continue, the first condition is false (Continue is in the exemption list), so execution falls through to the second check which then breaks. The first guard could simply be '!matches!(loop_flow, Normal)' and the second would be unreachable, or the logic restructured as a single match.
issues.suggestion: Replace with: 'match loop_flow { ControlFlow::Normal => {}, ControlFlow::Continue => break, _ => break, }' or more directly 'if !matches!(loop_flow, ControlFlow::Normal) { break; }' (since both Normal and Continue should proceed to the update step, but Continue should skip the rest of the body — the current code skips the update too when Continue fires via the inner for-body break).

issues.summary: pre_expand_variables() uses a manual char-indexed loop instead of idiomatic iterator/parser patterns
evidence: Lines 36-95: converts expr to Vec<char>, uses a mutable index i with while i < chars.len(), manually advances i for each character class — 60 lines of imperative scanning.
The rest of the codebase uses iterator chains and str methods; this function stands out as a style island.
issues.suggestion: Rewrite using str::char_indices() and a Peekable iterator, or use a small hand-rolled scanner struct that owns a Chars iterator. The core logic (skip $, read {var}, read positional, read identifier) maps naturally to a match on the next char with iterator lookahead.

issues.summary: sidebar builtin arm in execute_builtin dispatch is inlined with ad-hoc JSON/tuple logic while all other builtins delegate to named functions
evidence: Lines 281-296: the sidebar arm contains serde_json::to_string, tuple_space.out, and direct error printing inline in the dispatch match, unlike every other builtin which calls a dedicated builtin_xxx function.
This breaks the consistent extraction style that makes the match table readable.
issues.suggestion: Extract a builtin_sidebar(args: &[String], tuple_space: &TupleSpace) -> Result<BuiltinResult> function following the same pattern as all other builtins, and replace the inline block with a single delegation call.

issues.summary: from_definition() and configure_from_definition() in agent.rs duplicate identical logic for setting system_prompt and max_tokens from AgentDefinition
evidence: from_definition(): 'if !definition.prompt_template.is_empty() { config.system_prompt = ... } else if !definition.description.is_empty() { config.system_prompt = ... }'
configure_from_definition(): same if/else block on the same fields.
max_tokens assignment block also repeated.
issues.suggestion: Extract fn apply_definition_to_config(definition: &AgentDefinition, config: &mut AgentConfig) and call it from both methods.

issues.summary: is_colony_terminal() helper function is defined identically in both repl.rs and repl_tui.rs
evidence: repl.rs line 29-31: 'fn is_colony_terminal() -> bool { std::env::var("COLONY_TERMINAL").is_ok() }'
repl_tui.rs line 42-44: identical definition.

issues.summary: statement_to_shell_string falls back to format!("{:?}", expr) for ExprSub and unknown variants, embedding a Rust Debug string in production shell output
evidence: Line 49: 'WordPart::ExprSub(expr) => result.push_str(&format!("$[{:?}]", expr))'
Line 51: '_ => result.push_str(&format!("{:?}", p))' inside DoubleQuoted arm
Line 80: '_ => result.push_str(&format!("{:?}", other))' at top level
Line 275: 'other => format!("{:?}", other)' for unhandled Statement variants
Debug output (e.g., 'ExprSub { ... }') is not valid shell syntax and would cause re-parse failures if used in coproc or serialisation round-trips.
issues.suggestion: For ExprSub, implement a proper expression-to-string serialiser or at minimum return an empty string or a comment. For the catch-all Statement arm, consider a compile-time assertion that all variants are handled, or return an empty string with a tracing::warn rather than a Debug dump.

issues.summary: Agent.process() and Agent.process_full() implement the same loop independently with diverged accounting, persistence, and observation logic
evidence: process() records token usage via token_tracker.record() and saves messages to ConversationStore; process_full() skips token accounting and ConversationStore persistence entirely.
process_full() emits a ReflectionObserver observation at the end; process() does not.
Both methods clone messages, build a CompletionRequest, and push an assistant response — identical orchestration logic copied rather than shared.
process() delegates to cancellable_stream (a clean composable abstraction); process_full() drives the stream directly with while-let, duplicating the Done/Error/TextDelta handling.
issues.suggestion: Extract a private async fn run_completion_loop(&mut self, request: CompletionRequest, cancel: &CancellationToken) -> Result<String> that drives the stream and returns the full response text. Both process_with_cancellation() and process_full() call this shared core, then apply their own post-processing (token accounting, persistence, observation) in one place. This eliminates the risk of one path receiving a fix that the other silently misses.

issues.summary: Tool results are injected into message history as MessageRole::User with a plain-text prefix, making user messages structurally ambiguous
evidence: agent.rs line 612-615: after tool execution, a Message { role: MessageRole::User, content: MessageContent::Text(format!("Tool result: {}", result_str)) } is pushed to self.messages.
Any consumer that iterates self.messages cannot distinguish genuine user turns from synthetic tool-result turns without string-prefix inspection.
MessageContent already has a Blocks variant with ContentBlock::ToolResult; the provider layer understands this variant but it is not used here.
issues.suggestion: Use MessageContent::Blocks with a ContentBlock::ToolResult { tool_use_id, content } block to inject tool results. This keeps the message history structurally honest: consumers can match on role and content type without parsing text. The MessageRole should be User only for genuine user input; a distinct content type communicates the tool-result semantic without requiring a custom role.

issues.summary: AgentDefinition-to-AgentConfig translation logic is duplicated between from_definition() and configure_from_definition() with diverging control flow
evidence: Both from_definition() (lines 109-137) and configure_from_definition() (lines 140-183) contain the same model-spec parsing: split_once(':'), ProviderType::parse, infer_provider_from_model fallback.
from_definition() uses early-return Ok(Self::with_provider(...)) when a provider is parsed; configure_from_definition() uses let-binding with unwrap_or_else and calls switch_model separately.
configure_from_definition() checks temperature with is_some() before assigning, while from_definition() assigns unconditionally — a subtle behavioral difference that is not documented.
issues.suggestion: Extract fn apply_definition_to_config(definition: &AgentDefinition, config: &mut AgentConfig) -> Option<(ProviderType, String)> that applies all scalar fields and returns the parsed provider+model if present. Both from_definition() and configure_from_definition() call this helper, then each handles provider instantiation in its own way. This puts the translation in exactly one place.

issues.summary: DockerStatusComponent spawns a synchronous subprocess in render() instead of using the subscription/tuple mechanism, breaking the reactive boundary contract
evidence: DockerStatusComponent::render() calls std::process::Command::new("docker").args(["ps","-q"]).output() synchronously on every render invocation.
subscriptions() returns vec![] — the component declares no reactive dependencies, so the cache-invalidation mechanism cannot gate re-renders.

Every other builtin prompt component reads from the ComponentContext passed at the boundary (env vars, job counts, last_exit_code) without side-effectful I/O; docker_status is the only one that reaches outside the boundary.
issues.suggestion: Either (a) have a background poller emit a docker_status tuple to TupleSpace when container count changes, subscribe via subscriptions() to that pattern, and read the count from ComponentContext data rather than invoking docker at render time; or (b) add a poll_interval() override (e.g. 5 seconds) so the framework controls re-render frequency and make the I/O explicit. The key fix is that the render boundary should not perform blocking I/O that bypasses the subscription contract.

issues.summary: The 'sidebar' builtin in execute_builtin() is handled inline with a direct TupleSpace.out() call rather than through the dispatch pattern used by all other builtins
evidence: Lines 281-296 in the builtin match arm for 'sidebar': parse_sidebar_args is called, then serde_json::to_string and tuple_space.out() are invoked inline, bypassing the function-per-builtin pattern used by every other handler.
All other builtins (cd, export, flux, mirror, pane, etc.) are dispatched to a dedicated function: builtin_cd(), crate::flux::builtin_flux(), crate::panes::builtin_split(), etc.
The inline branch also calls unwrap_or_default() on the JSON serialization, silently swallowing serialization errors that would be surfaced as Err() in a dedicated function.
issues.suggestion: Move the sidebar logic into crate::sidebar::builtin_sidebar(&args, tuple_space) following the existing pattern, and replace the inline branch with a single dispatch call. This keeps the execute_builtin() dispatch table uniform and surfaces serialization errors through the Result<BuiltinResult> return type.
